subject: Hosted API pricing qualification - token volumes & peak TPS
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Cole <bethany@shoply.com>, Raj Singh <raj@shoply.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification - token volumes & peak TPS

Thanks again for the call today  great to learn more about Shoply's search + personalization rollout. Quick recap and a few asks so we can prepare a precise hosted API estimate: 

- Current ask: start with text-generation endpoints (intent classification + product personalization prompts).
- We need expected monthly token volume (1M tokens = standard unit for our hosted pricing), and how that breaks down between prompts vs completions (rough %).
- Peak load: what's your expected peak TPS and/or peak concurrent requests? Also helpful: typical request/response token lengths (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens).
- Budget: rough monthly budget range (helps us pick model/throughput guidance).
- Target unit economics: do you have a target $/1M tokens that you'd like to hit or benchmark against?

I attached a short template (pricing_estimate_template.xlsx)  if you can drop the token estimates there or paste them inline, that will speed up a formal quote.

Next step: once we get numbers, Ill loop in Alex (SE) to validate performance SLOs and confirm whether Hosted API normal mode will meet your peak TPS or if we should propose Dedicated capacity for predictable bursts.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachment: pricing_estimate_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Bethany Cole <bethany@shoply.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Singh <raj@shoply.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification - token volumes & peak TPS

Hi Marissa  thanks for the recap. Per our internal numbers (pulled a quick snapshot and attached):

- Expected monthly token volume: ~40,000,000 tokens/month (this is month 1 of roll-out; we expect 2-3x growth over 6 months).
- Prompt vs completion split: ~70% prompt / 30% completion by token count.
- Typical token lengths: avg prompt 60 tokens, avg completion 120 tokens.
- Peak TPS: ~45 TPS for short bursts during promos (sustained peak ~15 TPS). Peak concurrent requests roughly 12.
- Budget range: looking at $3,000  $7,000 / month initially (flexible if performance requires it).
- Target $/1M tokens: we'd like to aim for ~ $20 / 1M tokens or better if possible.

I've attached a CSV with a 14-day usage snapshot (shoply_usage_snapshot.csv). Happy to jump on a follow-up with Alex to validate throughput assumptions.

Thanks,
Bethany Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Recommendations | Shoply
bethany@shoply.com

Attachment: shoply_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Cole <bethany@shoply.com>, Raj Singh <raj@shoply.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification - token volumes & peak TPS

Thanks Bethany  this is very helpful. Quick reactions and next steps: 

- Volume: 40M tokens/month with 70/30 split and avg lengths you shared is a clear starting point  we can size hosted capacity for that and model unit economics.
- Peak TPS: 45 TPS short bursts is within what Hosted can absorb, though sustained peaks closer to ~15 TPS are the more relevant SLO for latency. If Shoply needs strict latency for every request at 45 TPS sustained, wed likely recommend Dedicated or a burst plan.
- Ballpark hosted pricing guidance (very rough, subject to model selection & contract tier):
   Base: $28 / 1M tokens (for standard open models we catalog)
   Compressed/quantized variants / higher commit: down to ~$18 - $22 / 1M tokens
   Discounts possible with committed monthly volume or a Dedicated capacity contract

Given your target of ~$20 / 1M tokens, there are credible paths to get there via commit tiers or model/quantization selection  Alex, can we schedule a 30-minute perf + architect call to validate payload sizes, latency SLOs, and whether Hosted will meet their burst needs?

Bethany/Raj  would Friday 2/27 at 10:00am PT work for a quick call? If not, send a couple of windows and Alex will join.

Cheers,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Hi all  happy to take this one. Friday 2/27 10:00am PT works for me. For the call Id like to validate a couple quick items so we can size the right throughput profile: 

- Typical JSON payload size and avg tokens per request (you mentioned 60/120 tokens  if you can share a sample request/response it helps).
- Acceptable tail latency %ile (p50/p95/p99) for the feature  e.g., p95 < 300ms or is 500ms OK?
- Are retries/backoffs handled client-side or would you prefer server-side queueing?

If Friday is confirmed Ill prepare a short perf run suggestion and a hosted vs dedicated delta summary so we can surface cost vs latency tradeoffs during the call.
